spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** An **LLM evaluation harness** is a versioned test runner that executes a prompt, RAG pipeline, or agent against a curated **golden dataset** (typically 200–500 stratified examples) and computes pass/fail gates across quality, latency, and cost.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Three-Tier Evaluation Gate Before Prompt Promotion (CI Runner -> LLM Pipeline -> Code Assertions -> LLM Judge); PR Gate -> Nightly Shadow Suite -> Human Calibration Store (PR CI Gate -> Nightly Replay -> Pinned Judge -> Human Audit).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Balance statistical precision against CI feedback speed and judge token cost. LLM outputs are stochastic, and a prompt edit that fixes one edge case routinely breaks three others silently.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Connect automated LLM evaluation to canary rollouts, prompt design, and LoRA distillation.

learningJourney.title: What is an LLM Evaluation Harness

explanation.foundation: An **LLM evaluation harness** is a versioned test runner that executes a prompt, RAG pipeline, or agent against a curated **golden dataset** (typically 200–500 stratified examples) and computes pass/fail gates across quality, latency, and cost.
explanation.core: Evaluation is organized into three tiers: **deterministic code assertions** (JSON Schema, regex, SQL execution), **reference-based metrics** (exact match, F1, semantic similarity), and **calibrated LLM-as-a-judge rubrics**.

learningJourney.title: Why prompt edits silently break production

explanation.foundation: LLM outputs are stochastic, and a prompt edit that fixes one edge case routinely breaks three others silently. Without an evaluation harness, teams ship regressions in JSON formatting, hallucinated citations, or latency spikes directly to users—only discovering them via support tickets.
explanation.core: In multi-step agent pipelines, silent 5% per-component regressions compound into broken end-to-end workflows.

ideas.title: Mitigating Judge Position & Verbosity Bias
ideas.description: LLM judges prefer the first option in pairwise A/B comparisons by 5–15% and favor longer answers. Randomize A/B order and score against explicit binary/Likert rubrics.

ideas.title: Preventing Eval Contamination
ideas.description: Maintain a held-out production shadow set refreshed monthly from real logs and never place held-out examples inside few-shot prompts.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement LLM Evaluation Harnesses without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When batching and tail latency compete for accelerator cycles, replace 'vibe checks' with a versioned golden dataset, deterministic code assertions, calibrated LLM-as-a-judge rubrics, and statistical confidence gates in CI/CD.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When LLM Evaluation Harnesses experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

knowledgeCheck.question: How do you prevent position bias when using an LLM-as-a-judge for pairwise A/B output comparison?

options.text: Always place the new candidate model in Position A
options.feedback: Placing the candidate consistently in Position A lets the 5–15% position bias inflate or deflate its score.

options.text: Run each comparison twice with A/B order swapped and average or require consistency across both passes
options.feedback: Correct: swapping A/B presentation order cancels out systematic first-position preference.

options.text: Use a floating 'latest' model alias for the judge
options.feedback: Floating aliases cause silent baseline drift over time; always pin judge snapshots.
